Domestic refineries imported 34.33 million barrels of crude oil between January and October 2026, representing 19.1 per cent of the 179.31 million barrels received by the facilities during the 10-month period. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority disclosed this in its October 2026 midstream and downstream statistics, which showed that locally sourced crude accounted for 144.98 million barrels, representing 80.9 per cent of total crude receipts. The data indicated that October recorded the highest monthly crude receipts within the period, as domestic refineries received 22.80 million barrels, comprising 19.13 million barrels of locally produced crude and 3.67 million barrels of imported supplies. The October volume represented a 23 per cent increase from the 18.53 million barrels recorded in September, when domestic refineries received 15.97 million barrels of local crude and 2.56 million barrels of imported crude. A monthly breakdown showed that crude receipts stood at 9.54 million barrels in January, comprising 8.83 million barrels of domestic crude and 710,000 barrels of imported supplies. In February, total receipts increased to 13.13 million barrels, comprising 8.88 million barrels of domestic crude and 4.25 million barrels of imported crude. The volume rose further to 20.92 million barrels in March, with local crude accounting for 11.49 million barrels and imports contributing 9.43 million barrels. In April, refineries received 18.37 million barrels, comprising 17.96 million barrels of domestic crude and 410,000 barrels of imported supplies. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. In June, the total increased to 19.12 million barrels, with domestic crude accounting for 17.08 million barrels and imported supplies contributing 2.04 million barrels. July recorded 17.88 million barrels, comprising 12.75 million barrels of domestic crude and 5.13 million barrels of imported supplies, while August recorded 21.10 million barrels, made up of 17.05 million barrels of local crude and 4.05 million barrels of imports. The regulator said crude oil receipts by domestic refineries rose 19 per cent to 0.74 million barrels per day in October, compared with 0.62 million barrels per day in September. The report further explained that imported crude supplies to the Dangote Petroleum Refinery increased 39 per cent to 118,400 barrels per day in October, reducing the share of locally sourced crude in its total intake to 83.9 per cent from 86.1 per cent in September. ‘Govs must take responsibility for power crisis’ Oil industry looking up Dangote IPO: SEC approves share allocation after 300% subscription It stated, “Crude oil receipts by domestic refineries rose 19 per cent to 0.736 mbpd (September: 0.617 mbpd). Imported crude to Dangote grew 39 per cent to 118,400 bpd, lowering the local crude share to 83.9 per cent from 86.1 per cent.” It also disclosed that the refinery received more crude than it processed during the month, reversing the trend recorded in September. “Dangote’s crude receipts exceeded its crude run by about 48,000 bpd, reversing September’s 71,000 bpd draw-down,” the NMDPRA stated. Meanwhile, the factsheet revealed that the Dangote refinery recorded no intake of intermediate products and gasoline blendstock in October. The facility received a cumulative 1.91 billion litres of the products between January and October, representing an average monthly intake of 191.04 million litres. January recorded the highest intake of 658.31 million litres, followed by May with 324.70 million litres and February with 306.89 million litres. The volume dropped to 102.35 million litres in March before increasing to 147.37 million litres in April. It rose further to 188.45 million litres in June but fell to zero in July. Intake resumed in August at 130.83 million litres before declining to 51.50 million litres in September and returning to zero in October. The NMDPRA explained that the absence of fresh blendstock receipts in October did not mean that previously received supplies were unavailable for use in domestic petroleum product production. It stated, “DPRP recorded no intermediates/gasoline blendstock intake in October 2026 (September: 51.50 ML). Blendstock received in earlier months, including imported cargoes, contributes to the domestic PMS volumes reported in this factsheet.” The regulator’s figures indicate that although domestic crude accounted for the bulk of refinery supplies during the 10 months, imported crude remained a significant source of feedstock, while the intake of intermediate products and gasoline blendstock by Dangote fluctuated considerably during the period. Dare Olawin Dare Olawin is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over a decade of reporting experience. He began his career as a community reporter and now covers the energy sector, including oil, gas, electricity, and renewables.
